title: 'Pick a date' with an empty date field silently creates or edits a link to NEVER expire
fix: In expiryControl: (1) change the line-532 change listener to also toggle required: `sel.addEventListener('change', () => { date.hidden = sel.value !== 'date'; date.required = sel.value === 'date'; });` — all four callers (newLinkForm ~561, openFolderPanel ~681, openDropPanel ~765, share edit ~719) submit via real <form> submit buttons, so the browser then blocks submit with 'Please fill out this field'. (2) Harden read() (line 533-535) so it can never emit -1 from an empty date: `if (sel.value === 'date') { const t = Date.parse(date.value); if (!t) { date.reportValidity(); throw new Error('Pick a date and time for the expiry.'); } return { expires_at: Math.floor(t / 1000) }; }`. (3) In openSharePanel's submit handler, move the `if (sel !== 'keep') Object.assign(body, exp.read());` line (~719) inside the existing try so a thrown read() lands in editErr instead of an unhandled rejection.
notes: Verified: app.js:533-534 returns { expires_hours: -1 } when Date.parse('')=NaN; server treats hours<0 as never (shares.go:283-289 leaves exp=0 on create; shares.go:348-350 sets expires=0 on PATCH). A user who explicitly picked a date to RESTRICT a link gets an immortal public link with no warning, in all four expiry forms. Two duplicate findings merged.

title: API-token Delete and 'Turn off two-factor' fire on a single un-confirmed click, unlike every other destructive button
fix: Apply the app's existing two-click dataset.armed pattern (as at app.js:737-741, 978-981, 1257-1260, 1519-1522, 1637-1640). Token delete (line 1119): `onclick: async ev => { const b = ev.currentTarget; if (!b.dataset.armed) { b.dataset.armed = '1'; b.textContent = `Delete “${t.name}”`; return; } await api('/api/tokens/' + t.id, { method: 'DELETE' }); closePanel(false); reload(); }`. 2FA reset (lines 975-977): change the handler to `async ev => { const b = ev.currentTarget; if (!b.dataset.armed) { b.dataset.armed = '1'; b.textContent = 'Really turn off two-factor'; return; } try { await api('/api/users/' + u.id, { method: 'PATCH', body: { reset_2fa: true } }); openUserPanel(id); viewUsers(getState(), routeSeq); } catch (x) { actErr.textContent = x.message; } }`.
notes: Verified: app.js:1119 deletes on first click; the token secret is shown only once (app.js:1098), so a misclick irrevocably severs every MCP client using it. app.js:975-977 strips a user's 2FA on one click. Every other danger button in the file arms first. Two duplicate findings merged.

title: boot() and the login submit have no error path: a failed /api/state or /api/login fetch leaves a permanently blank white page or a dead Sign-in button
fix: Wrap boot's body (app.js:137-144): `async function boot() { let st; try { const r = await fetch('/api/state'); st = await r.json(); } catch { gate(h('form', {}, h('h1', {}, h('img', { src: '/favicon.svg', alt: '' }), 'Burrow'), h('p', { class: 'err', role: 'alert' }, 'Can’t reach the server. Check Burrow and your network.'), h('button', { class: 'btn primary', type: 'button', onclick: () => boot() }, 'Retry'))); return; } ME = st; ... }`. In loginScreen's submit handler (app.js:165-166), wrap the fetch+json in try/catch and on failure set `err.textContent = 'Can’t reach Burrow — check your connection.'; return;`.
notes: Verified: index.html ships only an empty <div id="app">; boot() is called unguarded at module level (1244), from login success (167), setup (207), sign-out (1191), and every 401 inside api() (75) — a reverse-proxy 502 (non-JSON body makes r.json() reject) mid-session yields a blank page with no retry. Two duplicate findings merged.

title: Admin default expiry 0 ('never') is ignored: new-link dialogs preselect '7 days' instead of 'Never'
fix: In expiryControl change line 529 to: `const def = defHours === 0 ? '-1' : String(defHours || 168);`. Line 530's fallback keeps handling non-preset positive values. One line.
notes: Verified: `String(defHours || 168)` turns 0 into '168', which IS in opts, so the `defHours > 0 ? '168' : '-1'` fallback is unreachable for 0. Settings UI documents 0 as never (app.js:1172), and the server only honors it when the client sends expires_hours 0 (shares.go:285-288) — but read() sends the selected 168, so every UI-created link silently expires in 7 days against the admin's configuration.

title: Shared-folder admin upload: errors are invisible (message wiped by re-render, server reason discarded) and a network failure leaves 'Uploading…' stuck with a dead retry
fix: Rewrite the change handler body (app.js:638-646): `fileIn.addEventListener('change', async () => { if (!fileIn.files.length) return; const fd = new FormData(); for (const f of fileIn.files) fd.append('files', f, f.name); status.className = 'muted'; status.textContent = `Uploading ${fileIn.files.length} file${fileIn.files.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}…`; try { const r = await fetch(`/api/shares/${x.id}/upload`, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'X-Burrow': '1' }, body: fd }); if (r.ok) { changed(); } else { const d = await r.json().catch(() => ({})); status.textContent = d.error || `Upload failed (${r.status})`; status.className = 'err'; } } catch { status.textContent = 'Upload failed — connection lost'; status.className = 'err'; } finally { fileIn.value = ''; } });` — call changed() only on success, because changed() rebuilds the whole panel (openSharePanel → panelShell replaceChildren) and would wipe the error the instant it is set.
notes: Verified: current code sets 'Upload failed' then immediately calls changed(), which replaces the panel including the status node; the server's specific reason (collections.go:445 httpErr with err.Error(), e.g. 403 admins-only or 507 out-of-space) is never read; a rejected fetch is uncaught so 'Uploading…' sticks forever; fileIn.value is never reset so re-picking the same file fires no change event (the main uploader resets it at app.js:1314 for exactly this reason). Two duplicate findings merged.

title: Create forms never disable their submit button: a double click or double Enter mints two live share links (or drops/folders/users)
fix: In the four create submit handlers — newLinkForm (app.js:558), openFolderPanel (678), openDropPanel (762), openUserPanel create (952) — guard and disable: first lines `const b = f.querySelector('button[type=submit]'); if (b.disabled) return; b.disabled = true;` and wrap the existing body so a `finally { b.disabled = false; }` re-enables it. This is the exact pattern the remotes form already uses (app.js:1555-1558). base.css:91 already styles .btn[disabled].
notes: Verified: none of the four handlers disables the button while the POST is in flight; each extra POST /api/shares creates a separate ACTIVE link (shares.go createShare) that the user never sees, since the panel navigates to the first response's id.

title: Overview 'Rescan now' throws: e.currentTarget is null after await, so the confirmation never appears
fix: Capture the element before awaiting, like every other handler in the file (e.g. app.js:1606): `onclick: async e => { const b = e.currentTarget; b.disabled = true; await api('/api/rescan', { method: 'POST' }); b.textContent = 'Rescan started'; }` at app.js:824.
notes: Verified: event.currentTarget is reset to null once dispatch completes, which happens at the first await; the POST succeeds (api.go routes POST /api/rescan) but the assignment throws an unhandled TypeError, the label never changes, and the still-enabled button invites repeated rescans. Two duplicate findings merged.

title: Escape while typing in a panel form closes the panel and destroys everything typed
fix: In the global keydown handler (app.js:410-414), check `typing` before the panel branch: `if (e.key === 'Escape') { if (typing) { document.activeElement.blur(); return; } if (!$('#panel')?.hidden) { closePanel(); return; } return; }` — first Escape leaves the field, a second Escape closes the panel.
notes: Verified: the panel-close branch runs before the typing check, and closePanel() (app.js:445-450) does p.replaceChildren(), wiping the DOM — so Escape focused in any panel form field (new user with grants rows, new shared folder, new link, share edit, token editor) silently discards all input. The only-blur intent is visible on the very next line (412).

title: Entering a share password loses the deep link: the visitor is always dumped at the share root
fix: Carry p through the auth round trip: (1) in the two NeedPW renders (shares.go:588 and 599) set `Sub: cleanRel(r.URL.Query().Get("p"))` — for the 588 wrong-password re-render use `cleanRel(r.FormValue("p"))` since it is a POST; (2) in web/share.html add `{{if .Sub}}<input type="hidden" name="p" value="{{.Sub}}">{{end}}` inside the .pw form (after line 39); (3) on success (shares.go:595) build `dest := "/s/" + s.ID; if p := cleanRel(r.FormValue("p")); p != "" { dest += "?p=" + url.QueryEscape(p) }` and redirect to dest (add net/url to imports if missing).
notes: Verified: the password gate at shares.go:598-600 renders NeedPW without Sub, the form (share.html:37-42) carries no p, and success always redirects to "/s/"+s.ID — so a deep link to a specific file/subfolder in a protected folder share lands at the root after the password, and the visitor must re-find the file.

title: Public share page shows broken-image icons for HEIC/SVG/TIFF/RAW/PSD: it requests thumbnails the server can never make
fix: Add a FuncMap entry in shares.go:450-455: `"thumbable": func(e Entry) bool { return !e.IsDir && thumbExts[e.Ext] },` and in web/share.html:92 change `{{if eq .Kind "image"}}` to `{{if thumbable .}}` so unsupported formats fall through to the existing generic file SVG.
notes: Verified: Kind "image" covers 19 extensions (indexer.go kinds map: tif, tiff, heic, heif, svg, avif, raw, cr2, cr3, nef, arw, dng, psd...) but serveThumb supports only six (thumbs.go:30 thumbExts) and answers http.NotFound otherwise (thumbs.go:36-38). The logged-in app already guards this exact case (app.js:363). A shared folder of iPhone HEIC photos looks broken only on the public page.

title: Drop-page upload failures always say 'failed, try again', discarding the server's reason — even when the link is dead and retry can never work
fix: Resolve the XHR itself instead of a boolean: change line 51 to `x.onload = () => res(x);` and line 52 to `x.onerror = () => res(null);`, then after the await: `const good = x && x.status === 200; let msg = 'failed, try again'; if (x && !good) { try { msg = JSON.parse(x.responseText).error || msg; } catch { if (x.status === 410 || x.status === 404) msg = 'this link no longer works'; } }` and set `f._size.textContent = good ? 'sent' : msg;` (keep the existing className lines, which already use good).
notes: Verified: the server sends specific JSON reasons via httpErr (handleDrop → uploadErrCode: 507 'the server is almost out of space; try again later', 400 validation) and a dead link returns the HTML 410 state page from handleShare:558-560; share.js:51/56 throws all of it away, so visitors keep retrying an out-of-space or revoked drop.

title: Shared text/markdown/code files render a blank preview: previewKind returns "text" but the template has no text branch
fix: Add one branch after the pdf line in web/share.html (line 72): `{{else if eq .Preview "text"}}<iframe src="/s/{{.S.ID}}/raw{{if $p}}?p={{$p}}{{end}}" title="{{.File.Name}}"></iframe>` — the existing `.preview iframe` rule (share.css:10) already sizes it, and safeContentType (shares.go) already serves these as sandboxed text/plain.
notes: Verified: shares.go:784-786 classifies small code/txt/md/csv/log files as Preview "text", but share.html:69-73 only branches on image/video/audio/pdf, so a shared README.md shows an empty <div class="preview"> and forces a download. The raw fetch goes through the same gateDownload path the existing image/video previews use, so limit semantics are unchanged.

title: Asset cache-busting (?v=) is dead code: browsers run a stale app.js for up to 5 minutes after every upgrade and revalidate all assets every 5 minutes
fix: Version the URLs at serve time. In handleIndex (api.go:453-463), after reading index.html: `for _, n := range []string{"base.css", "app.css", "app.js"} { b = bytes.ReplaceAll(b, []byte("/assets/"+n+"\""), []byte("/assets/"+n+"?v="+version+"\"")) }` (version is main.go:25; add bytes to imports). For share.html (a Go template), add a FuncMap entry `"v": func() string { return version }` in shares.go:450 and change its three asset refs (lines 9, 10, 120) to e.g. `/assets/base.css?v={{v}}`. The existing immutable branch in handleAsset (api.go:477-481) then activates with no other changes.
notes: Verified: handleAsset already serves `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` when ?v= is present and max-age=300 otherwise, but index.html:8-10 and share.html:9-10,120 link assets bare, so after an upgrade a browser whose 300s cache is fresh runs the OLD app.js against the NEW API (index.html itself is no-cache); ServeContent also uses process startTime as Last-Modified (api.go:465,484), turning every restart into full re-downloads. Caveat: in dev builds version is "dev" — acceptable, or append startTime.Unix() for uniqueness.

title: route() refetches everything on every navigation: each row selection or arrow keypress fires 3 redundant requests and a full table+sidebar rebuild, and the sidebar is double-fetched at startup and refetched per search keystroke
fix: Three coordinated changes in route()/shell(): (1) delete the `loadNav();` call in shell() (app.js:244) — route() always runs right after boot and calls it; (2) in route(), gate loadNav on its inputs: module-level `let navKey = null;` then `const nk = s.view + '|' + s.path; if (nk !== navKey) { navKey = nk; loadNav(); }` (loadNav is still called explicitly where data changes: favBtn 482, settings save 1140, remotes 1522/1557); (3) short-circuit selection-only changes: module-level `let renderedKey = '';` and in route() after getState() compute `const key = [s.view, s.path, s.q, s.kind, s.sort, s.tab, s.within, s.add, s.user].join('\u0000');` — if `key === renderedKey && $('#content').childElementCount` skip the try/catch view dispatch entirely and fall through to the panel block at line 308 (openPanelFor already syncs row aria-selected at 462); set `renderedKey = key` after a successful view render and reset it (`renderedKey = '';`) in every path that mutates the listing and relies on route()/nav() refetching: uploadFiles (before its final route(), 1364), moveInto (1474), deleteControl success (1611), renameControl success (1590), the trash Restore/Delete handlers (1635, 1640), and newFolderControl success (1570).
notes: Verified: nav({sel}) on every row click (375) and arrow key (399) runs route(), which unconditionally calls loadNav() (292: /api/ls?path= + /api/favorites) and re-awaits the full view fetch (viewBrowse 313 or viewSearch 426) before the highlight applies — 3 HTTP requests and a full rebuild per keypress, lagging by a round trip on SMB/remote libraries (files.go:154-155 proxies listDir). shell()+route() at boot double-fetch the sidebar, and each search keystroke adds the two nav requests to /api/search. The reset list is essential: without it, delete/rename/upload/trash actions would stop refreshing the listing. Three overlapping findings merged.

title: Uploads cannot be cancelled: the tray's X only hides progress while multi-GB transfers keep running, though a cancel endpoint exists
fix: In uploadFiles (app.js:1330-1365): give each row a cancel flag and button — in the rows map add `const ctl = { aborted: false, ac: null };` and append `h('button', { class: 'iconbtn', 'aria-label': 'Cancel', onclick: () => { ctl.aborted = true; ctl.ac?.abort(); } }, icon('x'))` to the li; carry ctl in the returned object. In the transfer loop: before starting a row, `if (ctl.aborted) { st.textContent = 'Cancelled'; continue; }`; pass `signal: (ctl.ac = new AbortController()).signal` to the chunk PUT fetch (1347); in the inner catch, treat aborts as final: `if (x.name === 'AbortError' || ctl.aborted) throw Object.assign(new Error('Cancelled'), { final: true, cancelled: true, up });` before the retry logic. In the outer catch, when `x.cancelled` call `api('/api/uploads/' + (x.up?.id ?? up.id), { method: 'DELETE' }).catch(() => {})` and set st.textContent = 'Cancelled' without the err class.
notes: Verified: uploadFiles has no AbortController; the tray Close (app.js:1322) removes the DOM while the 8 MB chunk loop keeps PUTting. The backend supports cancel: DELETE /api/uploads/{id} → apiUploadCancel (writes.go:1177) and refuses new uploads at 100 open ones ('finish or cancel some first', writes.go:885), so abandoned uploads also pile toward that cap.

title: Links, Users and Activity rows are mouse-only: no keyboard path exists to open a share's details or a user at all
fix: Wrap each row's first-cell label in a real anchor (same pattern as the file table's dir links, app.js:379). viewShares (line 622): `h('a', { class: 'label', href: '?view=shares&share=' + x.id, onclick: ev => { ev.preventDefault(); ev.stopPropagation(); nav({ share: x.id }, true); } }, x.label || x.path)` in place of the label span. viewUsers (877): same with href `'?view=users&user=' + u.id` and `nav({ user: String(u.id), tab: '' }, true)`. Link-activity rows (790): make the share id cell an anchor to `'?view=shares&share=' + e.share + '&tab=all'`. File-changes rows (810): wrap the name label in an anchor (only when c.kind !== 'deleted') navigating as the row onclick does. `.files .name a` styling already exists (app.css:55-56) and anchors are focusable + Enter-activatable natively; keep the tr onclick for pointer users.
notes: Verified: these four tables set CURRENT = [] (613, 779, 871), so the global ArrowDown/Enter mechanism is dead there, and rows are bare tr onclick with no tabindex/anchor — the entire link-management and user-management flow is unreachable without a pointer (the only other route to a share panel is the Details anchor inside a file panel). Two duplicate findings merged; the anchor approach also gives middle-click/open-in-new-tab for free.

title: Moving a file is drag-and-drop only: impossible by keyboard and on phones, though the move API and progress plumbing already exist
fix: Add a moveControl(e) alongside renameControl in the panel's can_change row (app.js:497), modeled on renameControl (1580-1601): a 'Move' button that swaps to an input with its own datalist (`const options = h('datalist', { id: 'move-options' })`, filled via the existing folderSuggest(options, q) with the same debounced oninput/onfocus wiring as grantsEditor 898-899) plus Move/Cancel buttons; on confirm call the existing moveInto(e.path, dest.value.trim()) (app.js:1465), which already handles jobs, the progress tray and errors, then `panelFor = ''; nav({ sel: '' }, true);`. Guard with canMove(e.path, dest) before calling. ~20 lines, no new API.
notes: Verified: moveInto is called from exactly one place, the document drop handler (1432-1435), fed only by HTML5 drag — which Android Chrome never fires from touch and keyboards cannot drive. The panel offers Download/Open/Copy path/Favorite/Rename/Delete but no Move; renameControl cannot substitute (it rebuilds the path within the same parent, 1589). folderSuggest is reusable as-is (884-889).

title: Light-mode links and the current breadcrumb fail WCAG AA contrast (~3.6:1 and ~3.3:1)
fix: Add a text-safe accent token: in :root (base.css:19-37) add `--accent-text: oklch(0.53 0.13 70);`; in BOTH dark blocks (inside `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) :root:not([data-theme="light"])` at 38-54 and `:root[data-theme="dark"]` at 55-69) add `--accent-text: oklch(0.84 0.14 82);` (same as dark --accent). Then change base.css:74 to `a { color: var(--accent-text); }` and app.css:24 to `.crumbs b { color: var(--accent-text); }`. Buttons, focus rings, folder icons and nav fills keep --accent.
notes: Verified: --accent oklch(0.62 0.14 70) on --paper oklch(0.985...) computes to roughly 3.5:1, below the 4.5:1 AA threshold for the 15px/400 body text; .crumbs b sits on --surface and is worse. This hits every text link in light mode (Details, Folder fact, Download QR, Retry). Dark mode already passes (bright amber on black).

title: info() tooltips: text never announced to screen readers, one Escape kills all tips for keyboard users until re-render, and taps on touch screens can't open them
fix: Rework info() (app.js:63-65): `let tipId = 0; function info(text) { const id = 'tip-' + (++tipId); return h('button', { type: 'button', class: 'info', 'aria-label': 'More about this', 'aria-describedby': id, onclick: e => { const b = e.currentTarget; if ('open' in b.dataset) delete b.dataset.open; else b.dataset.open = ''; } }, 'i', h('span', { class: 'tip', id, role: 'tooltip' }, text)); }` (aria-describedby text is computed even while visibility:hidden). Beside the pointerover listener (app.js:67) add `addEventListener('focusin', e => { const b = e.target.closest?.('.info'); if (b) delete b.dataset.dismissed; });` and extend the Escape handler (66) to also `delete b.dataset.open`. In app.css next to line 124 add `.info[data-open] .tip { visibility: visible; }` and `.info::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset: -8px; }` for a 32px touch target on the 16px button.
notes: Verified: app.css:123-125 keeps .tip visibility:hidden except on :hover/:focus-visible — a tap triggers neither (buttons don't match :focus-visible on pointer activation), so all ~20 help texts (expiry semantics, token Ask/On modes, grant precedence...) are unreachable on phones, which base.css's own design notes name as a target; the aria-label masks the content and no describedby exists; the global Escape handler (66) sets data-dismissed on every .info and only pointerover (67) clears it, so after one Escape keyboard focus can never reveal a tip again. Two duplicate findings merged.

title: Enter or ArrowDown in the search box during the 110ms debounce/fetch window acts on the PREVIOUS view's rows, opening an unrelated folder
fix: In the search keydown handler (app.js:228-231), flush the pending navigation instead of acting on stale CURRENT (the debounce timer `t` is already in scope): `searchInput.addEventListener('keydown', e => { const v = searchInput.value.trim(); const s = getState(); const fresh = s.view === 'search' && s.q === v; if (e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); if (v && !fresh) { clearTimeout(t); nav({ view: 'search', q: v, sel: '' }, s.view === 'search'); } else openSel(); } if (e.key === 'ArrowDown' && fresh) { e.preventDefault(); moveSel(1); } });`
notes: Verified: the handler runs unconditionally while CURRENT is only replaced after the search response lands (viewSearch 438) and the nav itself is debounced 110ms (219-226); openSel falls back to CURRENT[0] (404), so typing a query and hitting Enter quickly opens the first entry of the folder you were browsing, then the pending debounce jumps to the results, leaving a junk history entry.

title: Text preview: an error body renders as the file's contents, a network failure shows 'Loading…' forever, and the whole file (up to 2 MB) is downloaded to show 20 KB
fix: Replace line 475's fetch chain: `fetch(raw, { headers: { Range: 'bytes=0-19999' } }).then(r => { if (!r.ok) throw new Error('Couldn’t load the preview.'); return r.text(); }).then(t => pv.textContent = t.slice(0, 20000)).catch(x => { pv.textContent = x.message; pv.className = 'muted'; });` — /api/raw ends in http.ServeContent (which honors Range with 206), and a server that ignored Range would return 200 with the full body, which the existing slice still handles.
notes: Verified: no r.ok check and no catch — a file deleted between /api/info and /api/raw shows the literal JSON error body as the file's text, and a rejected fetch leaves 'Loading…' with an unhandled rejection; previewKind allows text files up to 2 MB while only 20 KB is shown. Three overlapping findings (two error-handling duplicates + the Range efficiency one) merged into one 3-line change.

title: Every boot()/shell() stacks another never-cleared 15s /api/status poller; stale ones keep polling after sign-out
fix: Module-level `let footTimer = 0;` and in shell() replace line 246 with `clearInterval(footTimer); footTimer = setInterval(refreshFoot, 15000);`. Optionally add `if (document.hidden) return;` as refreshFoot's first line plus a visibilitychange listener that calls refreshFoot() when the tab becomes visible, so hidden tabs stop polling.
notes: Verified: the interval id at app.js:246 is never stored; shell() runs on every successful boot, and boot() re-runs on sign-in (167), setup (207), sign-out (1191) and any 401 in api() (75) — N sign-in/out cycles leave N concurrent pollers, which keep hitting /api/status quietly from the login screen (refreshFoot's catch at 279 swallows everything). Two duplicate findings merged.

title: Armed danger buttons never disarm: 'Delete forever', 'Delete link', 'Remove phone' etc. stay armed indefinitely, so a much later stray click fires instantly
fix: Add one helper near deleteControl: `function armOnce(b, label) { if (b.dataset.armed) return true; b.dataset.armed = '1'; const old = [...b.childNodes]; if (b.lastChild.nodeType === 3 || !b.querySelector('span')) b.textContent = label; else b.lastChild.textContent = label; const reset = () => { if (!b.isConnected || !b.dataset.armed) return; delete b.dataset.armed; b.replaceChildren(...old); }; b.addEventListener('blur', reset, { once: true }); setTimeout(reset, 4000); return false; }` and convert the seven sites to `if (!armOnce(b, 'Delete …')) return;`: share delete (737-741, also re-hide purge in reset path or leave it visible — harmless), collection upload delete (653-655), user delete (979-981), device remove (1258-1260), remote remove (1520-1522), file delete (1606-1607, which uses b.lastChild to keep its icon), trash delete-forever (1638-1640).
notes: Verified: nothing ever deletes dataset.armed at any of the seven sites — no blur, timeout or pointer-leave — so an armed 'Delete forever' (unrecoverable) fires on a single click minutes later. Mitigated by the visible label change, hence P3. Implementer note: the file-delete site mutates b.lastChild.textContent to preserve its icon; the helper must restore original child nodes, not plain text.

title: In-app form errors and 'Saved' confirmations are silent for screen readers (only login/setup have role=alert)
fix: Add `role: 'alert'` to each err element and `role: 'status'` to each saved element at creation. Simplest: two helpers near h() — `const errEl = (tag = 'p') => h(tag, { class: 'err', role: 'alert' });` and `const savedEl = () => h('span', { class: 'saved', role: 'status' });` — and use them at the ~14 sites: new link err (548), collection add err (509), folder-panel err (668), share edit editErr/saved (698-699), drop err (754), user err/saved (936-937), user actErr (970), token err/saved (1032-1033), settings section err/saved (1134-1135), remotes err (1544), 2FA err (1196), newFolder/rename/delete inline errs (1567, 1584, 1604). An empty alert element whose textContent is later set announces reliably.
notes: Verified: only app.js:152/176/190 carry role=alert; every other async form writes failure/success into bare elements, so a screen-reader user submitting any share, user, token or settings form hears nothing either way (WCAG 4.1.3). Pure attribute additions, zero behavioral risk.
